content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents to solve multiple video recognition tasks in different settings (i.e., close-set, long-tail, few-shot, and open-set settings) with a single framework, which uses web text to facilitate training and perhaps inference. The framework employs two-stage training; the first stage is pre-training to adopt the CLIP backbone to the dataset, and the second stage is finetuning the model with the ground-truth labels. The experimental results show significant performance boosts in some tasks. Ablation studies are provided as well that cover some aspects of the framework.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
#### Strengths

The experimental results show substantial improvement compared to previous methods in some tasks. Although there should be some arguments about the fairness of using web text for training (and inference), the performance boosts look nice. 

The framework is relatively simple, yet the performance increases a lot, which implies the effectiveness of the idea of using web text and the method for training the model. 

#### Weaknesses

One thing I cannot find in the paper is which web text is used for training (and inference); that is, which $\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{T}$ are used may not be specified. Since the web text is curated based on ground-truth labels, they almost serve as ground-truth labels. Therefore, I don’t think it’s fair to compare the proposed framework with existing methods if they are used in training and inference. I believe at least for the few-shot and open-set setting, in which ground-truth labels are not available, the corresponding web text should not be used. I would like to have clarification on this point, and if the method would use them for training and inference, strong justification would be necessary. 

The ablation studies in the supplementary material show that CLIP is the most important component to improving performance. This result somehow spoils the significance of the paper. I think the close-set setting, which is the setting with which the ablation is done, gets the minimum impact from not using CLIP, so I would like to see how it affects other settings.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper basically is well-written but I had some difficulties in understanding the methodology part (including the unclarity mentioned in the weakness section above). The presentation of the paper could be improved. Also, due to the reason in the weakness section, the reproducibility of the paper is limited (I don’t think one can reproduce the same results without code being published). 

The idea of using web text in classification tasks itself is not new as I can find some work like [Wang and Mao, “Learning Semantic Text Features for Web Text-Aided Image Classification,” TMM, vol. 21, no. 12, 2019] to facilitate classification with help of web text. But the application seems still new and I think that showing the simple framework improves the performance a lot can contribute to the community.
content.summary_of_the_review: I like the paper’s idea, but the unclarity mentioned in the weakness section seems critical to me. This point should be clarified in the discussion period.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper (a) builds a comprehensive video recognition benchmark of Kinetics-GVR that includes 4 sub-task datasets, (b) presents a unified visual-linguistic framework that includes two-stage training (contrastive pretraining + language-drive finetune). It achieves excellent performance on four datasets (Kinects-close/LT/fewshot/open).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. Building a comprehensive video recognition benchmark.
2. Achieving excellent performance, outperforming baseline.

Weakness:
1. Lack of technical novelty. The first stage (Visual-language contrastive pretraining) is not new. The second stage (text selection ruler TSR) is difficult to be considered as a technical innovation. I understand that this paper has multiple contributions like building benchmark and framework, but novelty is not equal to sum of all contributions.  

2. It is not clear about the "contribution of this paper" vs "contribution of CLIP".  In ablation (Table 7), the most important part is CLIP weights. Also in Table 9, using CLIP model for KD is also crucial. I would be better to clear indicate "what is the additional contribution of this paper on top of CLIP".
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well written. It should not be hard to reproduce. The major concern is lack of novelty and clarification between the contribution of this paper and contribution of CLIP.
content.summary_of_the_review: Reject is rated, due to the lack of novelty and contribution beyond CLIP. Innovation and clear description of contribution are crucial for top conference like ICLR.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper the authors present a solution for general video recognition: a system that is able to deal with different settings such as close-set, long-tail, few-shot and open-set. The contribution of the paper is two fold: building of a video recognition benchmark; a deep learning architecture.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The addressed topic is timely. 
- The paper is well-structured and it's easy to read

Weaknesses
- The contribution of the paper is not highlighted enough and not so clear. 
In particular for the benchmark, the authors define some categories (close-set, long-tailed, few shot open-set) and the populate them with videos from Kinetics-400. They also add data description using Wikipedia and wikiHow. 
The first issue: why do the authors decide to define these categories and not others? In the introduction the authors stress that some other benchmarks introduce domain bias. What kind of actions do the authors perfom in order to reduce possible bias in their benchmark? 

For the proposed solution, first is not clear for me the contribution in the architecture with respect to the related work. Second, why does the proposed architecture should better address different video settings (close-set, long-tail, few-shot and open-set)?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: As said, the paper is well-structured and easy to follow. Novelty should be better described. For the reproducibility, the authors describe several implementation details and they also write they will release the code in the future.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is well-written and well-structured. The novelty and the motivation are not highlighted enough.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
